title: Trump Wants an 'AI Force' — and a Special AI Boss
summary:
Imagine a whole team in the government whose only job is artificial intelligence — AI. That's what President Donald Trump says he wants to build. He calls it the 'AI Force,' and he wants to put one special boss in charge: an AI tsar.

Trump shared the plan in a social media post on Saturday. He said his team 'will not in any way hinder or stifle' AI — meaning he won't slow it down. He also said AI is 'the next Industrial Revolution, or Internet, but will be even larger.' He even guessed it could become 25% of America's GDP. GDP is the total money a country makes in a year — so that's a giant slice of the pie.

Why does he care so much? Trump says he wants the U.S. to stay ahead of China in AI.

But not everyone agrees. Some AI leaders, like Dario Amodei of Anthropic, want AI to slow down until it's safer. Trump calls those worries a 'hoax' — something fake. He says the government will go after people who use AI to do bad things.

Trump meets China's President Xi Jinping next week, and AI is expected to come up.
why_it_matters: AI is already inside the apps, games and tools kids use every day, so choices made now about how fast it grows and who watches it will shape the world they grow up in.

background_read: Artificial intelligence, or AI, means computer programs that can learn and do jobs that used to need a human brain, like writing, drawing, or answering questions.
US presidents have long given special helpers nicknames ending in 'czar' — such as a 'drug czar' in charge of fighting drugs. 'Tsar' was the old word for a Russian king.

The first Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the 1700s, when steam engines and factories changed how people worked and lived all over the world. Trump says AI could be an even bigger change than that.

WHERE: Announced in a social media post in the United States, ahead of a meeting with China's leader.
WHY: Trump wants the US to stay ahead of China in AI and says he will not slow the technology down.

perspectives.description: Trump says AI is the next Industrial Revolution and could make up a quarter of America's GDP, so the government should race ahead and not hinder it.
Some AI leaders, like Dario Amodei of Anthropic, want AI to slow down until it is safer, because they worry about the risks it could bring.
Others note that Trump calls safety worries a 'hoax' but also says the government will go after people who use AI to do bad things.
